facts.content: Patient reports worsening of itchy, sore, red skin rash.
facts.source_text: CC: Worsening itchy, sore, red skin rash

facts.content: The rash has been present for a few days and is widespread on chest, hands, and arms.
facts.source_text: HPI: Few days; widespread on chest, hands, arms

facts.content: The worst areas are in the antecubital fossae.
The rash is very pruritic and dry with cracked areas.
facts.source_text: very pruritic and dry; cracks present

facts.content: Patient denies weeping from the rash.
Patient reports no fever or joint pains.
Patient has a history of eczema.
Patient has a history of asthma.
Patient uses Diprobase cream.
Patient uses a dermal wash in the shower.
Patient has tried over-the-counter hydrocortisone.
Patient previously tried over-the-counter antihistamine like cetirizine, which was ineffective.
Patient is not currently on antihistamines.
Uses blue inhaler for asthma as needed.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient's mother has migraine and hypothyroidism.
Diagnosis of atopic dermatitis flare, extensive, with a pruritic, erythematous, dry rash, especially flexural.
facts.source_text: Atopic dermatitis flare, extensive—widespread pruritic, erythematous, dry rash esp flexural (antecubital)

facts.content: The rash is refractory to OTC hydrocortisone and OTC antihistamine.
facts.source_text: refractory to OTC hydrocortisone and OTC antihistamine

facts.content: Patient is afebrile and systemically well.
Asthma is intermittent and currently stable.
Start fexofenadine, an antihistamine, with the dosing and frequency not specified.
Apply Betnovate, a topical steroid, thin layer twice daily for about 2 weeks.
facts.source_text: Start Betnovate (topical steroid): thin layer (fingertip unit), BID x ~2 weeks

facts.content: Continue using Diprobase and dermal soap substitute.
facts.source_text: Continue emollients: Diprobase and “dermal” soap substitute

facts.content: Safety net: instructs to contact if the condition worsens within 2 weeks, no improvement after treatment trial, or if there are adverse reactions.
facts.source_text: Safety net: contact if worsening within 2 wks, no improvement after trial, or any adverse reaction

facts.content: Prescription to be sent to Boots pharmacy.
Continue using the blue inhaler for asthma PRN and monitor symptoms.
facts.source_text: Continue blue inhaler PRN; monitor symptoms
